Risk of falls from greater than 2 metres.job_step: Access workface from mobile scaffold or platform ladder
Risk of falls from greater than 2 metres.hazards:
Hazard: Access to workface

Risk: Fall from heights, striking personnel/ objects, electric shock, injury
Risk of falls from greater than 2 metres.controls:
(Dis)assembly to be carried out by a competent person. Scaffolds above 4 metres to be erected by ticketed scaffolder only.
Stay within safety rails and observe SWL
Tools to be placed in receptacles
Ensure hose and tools are secured or contained
Do not use on unlevel surfaces or overload platform with material. All feet must be securely positioned on the ground
Three points of contact whilst climbing a ladder
Do not use conductive platforms near electrical work 
Do not step above the platform, overreach, or use a ladder whilst closed

Risk of falls from greater than 2 metres.hazards:
Hazard: MEWP

Risk: Worker, material fall from height. Crush
Risk of falls from greater than 2 metres.controls:
Operators to have ticket of competency for scissor lift
Stay within the platform and do not climb the sides
Use spotter when moving or working near live services
Place an exclusion zone with signage around scissor lift in all potential drop zones
Observe wind rating and SWL. Do not elevate in high winds.
Ensure hose and tools are secured- lanyards must be attached to all tools
Ensure daily logbook is completed
Ensure scissor lift is inducted with the principal contractor and plant risk assessment provided
Operator to be aware of and check blind spots
Wheel stops must be installed at all slab edges and penetrations before scissor lift is used
Check that any suspended area is rated to take the load
Do not drive across an incline
Ensure scissor lift is turned off, isolated, and keys removed at the end of each day
Traffic management plan in place if scissor lift is driven on a road.

Risk of falls from greater than 2 metres.hazards:
Hazard: MEWP

Risk: Worker, material fall from height. Crush
Risk of falls from greater than 2 metres.controls:
Operators to have HRWL for boom lifts over 11m and must always wear a secured harness 
Stay within the platform and do not climb the sides 
Use spotter when moving or working near live services
Do not approach perimeter edges without a zone permit
Place an exclusion zone with signage around EWP in all potential drop zones
Observe wind rating and SWL. Do not elevate in high winds.
Ensure hose and tools are secured- lanyards must be attached to all tools
Ensure safety harness and lanyard have 6-month inspections in place and register of inspection provided to the principal contractor
Ensure daily logbook is completed
Ensure EWP is inducted with the principal contractor and plant risk assessment provided
Operator to be aware of and check blind spots
Wheel stops must be installed at all slab edges and penetrations before EWP is used
Check that any suspended area is rated to take the load
Do not drive across an incline
Ensure EWP is turned off, isolated, and keys removed at the end of each day
Traffic management plan in place if EWP is driven on a road

Risk of falls from greater than 2 metres.hazards:
Hazard: Access to workface

Risk: Trapped or injured worker
Risk of falls from greater than 2 metres.controls:
All workers to practice use of ground controls for each EWP
One ground-based worker to be present to operate controls if needed
If a worker is trapped or injured assess the incident
Call out to persons inside the EWP
Only approach if safe to do so
Raise the alarm
Lower using ground controls
Call “000” in an emergency and follow the Emergency Response Plan

Work that involves the cutting of crysta.hazards:
Hazard: Failure to establish exclusion zones.

Risk: Nearby workers exposed to silica dust.
Work that involves the cutting of crysta.controls:
- Set up exclusion zone and signage

- Restrict access to other workers

Work that involves the cutting of crysta.hazards:
Hazard: Movement of equipment

Risk: Personal Injury
Work that involves the cutting of crysta.controls:
- Obey all signage and directions

- Use correct lifting techniques and mechanical aids where possible

- Do not lift over 20kg alone, use two men or mechanical aid

- Inspect electrical tags and ensure tags are up to date

- Workers must have silica awareness training

- Workers to conduct annual fit test training for respirators

- Workers to conduct annual health monitoring

- Respirators are regularly checked & maintained

Work that involves the cutting of crysta.hazards:
Hazard: Faulty or untested dust extraction system

Risk: High airborne dust concentration
Work that involves the cutting of crysta.controls:
- Inspect and test machine extraction, and HEPA filters before use

- Replace filters when needed

Work that involves the cutting of crysta.hazards:
Hazard: Inhalation of Dust

Risk: Respiratory Harm
Work that involves the cutting of crysta.controls:
- Enforce Correct PPE

- Wear P3 Respirators

- Check Respirator filters and replace when needed

Work that involves the cutting of crysta.hazards:
Hazard: Silica Dust produced by equipment 

 

 Risk: Inhalation of Silica Dust
Work that involves the cutting of crysta.controls:
- Set up dust control tent, air filtration system and HEPA Filter
 - Place machinery within exclusion zone
 - Provide and enforce correct PPE and P3 Respirators
 - Inspect tools and equipment before use
 - Strictly limit access to the exclusion zone while works are in progress

Work that involves the cutting of crysta.hazards:
Hazard: HEPA Filter requiring replacement

 

 Risk: Silica Dust escaping the filters.
Work that involves the cutting of crysta.controls:
- Inspect Air Filtration unit gauge to determine if HEPA Filter is full

 - Replace HEPA Filters as required

 - Replace P3 Respirator filters as required 

 - Bag and seal filters for disposal

Work that involves the cutting of crysta.hazards:
Hazard: Silica Dust produced by Sweeping

Risk: Inhalation of Silica Dust
Work that involves the cutting of crysta.controls:
- Use of P3 Respirators while cleaning/sweeping

 - Wet dust before sweeping

 - Use an M or H class Vacuum unit

 - Bag and Seal collected dust for disposal

Work that involves the cutting of crysta.hazards:
Hazard:  Incorrectly removing contaminated gear

Risk: Cross-contamination to clean areas
Work that involves the cutting of crysta.controls:
- Follow proper doffing sequence

- Bag disposable PPE

- Wash reusable gear separately.
